column1: # WHICH BioNumbers RECORDS ARE CONCENTRATIONS, and what compound each one is about.
# THIS FILE MAPS IDENTITY, NEVER VALUES. The number and its unit are read from the pinned
# record; this table says only "BNID N is a concentration of compound X". BioNumbers rows
# carry an organism and free text and no chemical identifier at all, so something has to
# supply the identifier, and doing it here -- one line per BNID, checkable against the
# pinned record's own description -- is the narrowest place to put it.
# WHY THIS IS NOT A CURATED CONCENTRATION TABLE. Every value still comes from a cited
# record under the same measured-only rule ECMDB is held to. What is hand-made is the
# assertion that a given BNID is about O2, which BioNumbers does not state machine-readably.

column5: Oxygen solubility in M9 medium at 37 C -- the growth medium and temperature this reference universe assumes
Oxygen concentration in air-saturated aqueous buffer at 37 C -- a second condition, which is what gives the pool a measured width instead of a floored one
